The '''2025–26 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Alabama]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Crimson Tide, led by seventh-year head coach [[Nate Oats]], played their home games at [[Coleman Coliseum]] located in [[Tuscaloosa, Alabama]] as a member of the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]].

==Previous season==
The [[2024–25 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Crimson Tide]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] with a record of 28–9, 13–5 in SEC play to finish in third place. In the [[2025 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they defeated [[2024–25 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] in the quarterfinals before falling to [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] for a second year in a row, this time in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the number two seed in the East Region, where they defeated [[2024–25 Robert Morris Colonials men's basketball team|Robert Morris]] in the first round, [[2024–25 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team|Saint Mary's]] in the second round and [[2024–25 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|BYU]] in the Sweet Sixteen before falling to [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the Elite Eight.<ref>{{cite web |title=2024-25 Alabama Crimson Tide Men's Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/alabama/men/2025-schedule.html |website=Sports Reference |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>

Former Alabama center [[Charles Bediako]] made a brief return to the Crimson Tide during the season while on a temporary restraining order. He attempted to regain college eligibility to play out one final college season. He appeared in five games between January 24 and February 7, helping the team go 3–2 over that stretch.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Medcalf |first2=Myron |title=What the Charles Bediako ruling means for Alabama and future NCAA eligibility cases |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/47881827/charles-bediako-ruling-alabama-future-ncaa-eligibility-cases-2026 |access-date=10 February 2026 |work=ESPN.com |date=9 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>
